articleTitle: Comparative Study of Different Combinations of Metalized Flexible Shielding Materials Under Mechanical Stress
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The characterisation of shielding materials under different measuring conditions is still a difficult topic. In this paper, some measuring results will be discussed for flexible metalised materials under mechanical stress conditions. In a first part, the basic concept of both TEM-t and H-t cells is summarised. The TEM-t cell has been designed for plane wave conditions, and the H-t cells is usable for magnetic field, near field condition. Concerning the samples to be used, both cells are compatible and easy to use, without any specific preparation of the samples. Due to their design, orientation and field polarisation effects can be studied. This property is a big advantage when studying discontinuities in the material. In a second part, the use of these test methods will be discussed for the characterisation of metallised woven and non-woven materials and their use in applications, where plying and folding the material is an essential part of the application. In a third part, the influence of the mechanical stress conditions on corrosion is studied.

articleTitle: Radiated Emission Estimation by Measurement of Magnetic Near Fields
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper presents a technique to estimate radiation from a DUT by means of samples of magnetic field amplitude only, and therefore the method does not require one to model the source. After reconstructing the phase of the samples by a simple algorithm, the field distribution is computed by the cardinal series over a sphere enclosing the DUT. Finally a spherical wave expansion is adopted to represent the radiated field in each point of the space outside the sphere. The effectiveness of the method is tested by simulations and by comparison of estimated and measured fields of a radiating PCB.

articleTitle: Comments on the Line Injection Method for Measuring Surface Transfer Impedance of Cables
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Experimental measurements and theoretical analysis were used to show that the line injection method for measuring surface transfer impedance was equivalent to methods that used a drive line that fully enclosed the cable under test. In addition, the far end line injection method was capable of making credible measurements to more than an order of magnitude higher frequency than the quadraxial test fixture when the same length sample was used. The transition between the low and high frequency regimes was small (less than an octave). A 2.1 cm diameter cable shield made of perforated copper sheet had a transfer impedance that was about an order of magnitude greater than the equivalent sized braided cable.

articleTitle: A 9 Channel Photonic Isotropic Electric and Magnetic Field Sensor With Sub-Nanosecond Rise Time.
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: One of the main obstacles to develop isotropic high frequency field sensors are the enormous difficulties to miniaturize the sensor head simultaneously providing sufficient sensitivity, dynamic range and electrical isolation. This paper will present a recent prototype development of a fully triaxial photonic field probe for transient and continuous wave electric and magnetic field measurements. The probe head incorporates nine electrooptic Lithium Niobate (LiNbO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>) modulators packaged in purely dielectric material. The modulators cover a frequency range from dc to 3.5 GHz, where in the range dc to 1 GHz an amplitude flatness of ± 0.5 dB can be specified.

articleTitle: Lightning Electromagnetic Fields: Modeling and Measurements
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Modeling of lightning return strokes as sources of electromagnetic fields is reviewed. Validation of the models using measured fields due to natural and triggered lightning is discussed.

articleTitle: Shielding Effectiveness Prediction in Low-Frequency Low-Impedance Source Configurations
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Some aspects related to shielding effectiveness (SE) prediction are analyzed. In particular consequences of the approximation of real sources as elemental dipoles are considered. Classical Schelkunoff approach is revisited in order to assess its applicability in configurations described by standards and its limits are outlined. The accuracy of the small dipole approximation in close proximity of the source is analyzed with reference to geometrical configurations described by standards.

articleTitle: On the Characterization of the Electromagnetic Field in Reverberating Chambers
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A stochastic characterization of the electromagnetic field within a reverberating chamber is here illustrated. It is shown how such an approach permits one to describe this field, which is stochastic in nature, in a compact, meaningful and effective manner. In particular, a first-order and second-order characterization is employed in order to achieve some physical insights. A set of illustrative experiments are also shown and discussed. They test the Istituto Universitario Navale chamber behaviour at 500 MHz and 10 GHz.

articleTitle: Prediction Errors Due to Ignoring Field Coupling on Printed Circuit Boards
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper deals with the coupling between traces on Printed Circuit Boards (PCB). Particularly a method is presented which allows to estimate the deviation of the current distribution on an active trace due to the omission of recoupling by an adjacent trace. An effective characteristic impedance for the active trace is deduced by the use of the model of capacitive coupling. The comparison with the characteristic impedance of a single trace enables the estimation of the maximum error of the current distribution. The method is examined with real life configurations on PCB.

articleTitle: On-Chip Measures to Achieve EMC
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Compliance with EMC requirements has to be reached at product level. For economic reasons measures need to be taken at the PCB and even better at the IC level to obtain an optimal result. In IC industry, a lot of measures are known but not made public. In this paper a number of general on-chip measures in combination with their PCB application will be reported. The defined models can also be used to predict RF emission with a certain measurement method. However, the selection of the test method has a great influence on the perceivability of the measures taken.

articleTitle: Effects of Power Converter Parasitic Components on Conducted EMI
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper deals with conducted Electromagnetic Interference (EMI) produced by power electronic converters. Both differential and common-mode components of the conducted emissions are considered. In particular, the analysis is focused on converters controlled with PWM techniques and supplied by a DC source. A circuit model which takes account of parasitic components is proposed for a switching cell that is the basic structure of this kind of converters. The values of the parasitic parameters (inductances and capacitances) are obtained by measurements, field analysis or both. This model permits the influence of the different parasitic parameters to be investigated. The simulations carried out by PSpice are compared with the corresponding experimental data obtained from a DC chopper prototype. The good agreement between the numerical and experimental results proves that the proposed equivalent circuit allows the prediction of the main conducted EMI phenomena with sufficient accuracy.

articleTitle: Reduction of Circuit Complexity using Tensor Analysis of Networks
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The authors have developed a technique that allows one to automatically derive simple full wave equivalent lumped networks for general planar interconnection discontinuities. In this technique, we start from a so called partial element description (PED) of the given structure, which is a network interpretation of the numerical analysis of the given structure, analogous to Ruehli’s PEEC method. Then, this PED is reduced using a very general network reduction technique, which was also developed by the same authors. In this paper, we will focus on the network reduction scheme.

articleTitle: An Antenna Theory Model for the Lightning Return Stroke
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A new approach, based on antenna theory, is used to evaluate the lightning return-stroke current as a function of time and height. The lightning channel is modeled as a lossy, straight, and vertical monopole antenna above a perfectly conducting ground, and is fed by a source voltage. The source voltage is a function of the assumed current at ground level and the input impedance of the monopole antenna. An electric field integral equation (EFIE) is employed to describe the electromagnetic behavior of the anteima. The numerical solution of EFIE by the Method of Moments (MoM) in time domain provides the time-space distribution of the current along the lightning channel. This new antenna-theory model with specified current at the channel base requires only two adjustable parameters: the return-stroke propagation speed and the channel resistance per unit length. The new model is compared to the most commonly used lightning return-stroke models in terms of the temporal-spatial distribution of channel current and predicted electric fields.

articleTitle: An EMC Diagnostic Method for Reverse Modeling of a Radiating Source using GTEM Readings
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper describes a new approach to EMC diagnosis using the near-field terms available from GTEM emissions readings. GTEM readings measure a fundamentally different quantity from OATS readings. On an OATS the far-field, field strength is measured. In a GTEM the nearfield, radiated power is the measured quantity. The inherent information contained in each of these quantities is different. GTEM readings carrying much more information about the radiating source than do OATS readings. By exploiting this difference a great deal of diagnostic insight about the radiating source may be gained.

articleTitle: The Common-Mode Skeleton Model for Assessment of Electromagnetic Compatibility at the System Level
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility

authors.preferredName: G. P. J. F. M. Maas
M. J. C. M. van Doom

abstract: A system-level approach is presented to predict the electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) of a system in an early design phase. It is based on the commonmode skeleton model: all cables are represented by single-wire models and each printed circuit board (PCB) is replaced by a (simplified) model representing its electromagnetic characteristics. The parameters needed for the PCB models can be measured using simple workbench methods or can be extracted from simulations of individual PCB’s.

articleTitle: Simulation Methods for Radiation Analysis of Transmission Line Structures on PCB
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Due to the increasing frequency of digital and/or analog signals the problem of high frequency radiation has become of serious concern to manufacturers and designers of electronic products. One of the most important aspects of ’ElectroMagnetic Compatibility’ (EMC) is the compliance with radiation constraints (CISPR, FCC). In order to predict the radiation of Printed Circuit Boards (PCB), all relevant effects related to nearby concucting structures must be taken into consideration. Often splitted ground and powerplanes are designed, which makes it very difficult to get a detailed insight into the overall signal and radiation behaviour. In this paper a numerical technique will be presented which is capable to analyse those structures concerning their electromagnetic behaviour. The problem is described by means of the ‘Electric Field Integral Equation’ (EFIE) within the frequency domain. An approximate solution of the integral equation is obtained by applying the Method of Moments (MOM). Using this approach a full wave solution is available for nearly arbitrary geometrical structures of the conducting regions on a PCB.

articleTitle: Transmission Cross Section of Apertures Determined by Measurements and FDTD Simulations
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Knowledge of the transmission cross section of apertures, σ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">a</inf>, constitutes an important factor in design and analysis of electrically large shielded structures. This paper presents a comparison between measured and calculated (FDTD) results of σ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">a</inf> for several apertures. The FDTD simulations are based on a routine that calculates the Poynting vector on a surface behind the aperture. The measurements are based on the use of a overmoded cavity backing the aperture. The results show good agreement, also with an exact solution.

articleTitle: EMC-Effects on Integrated Circuits
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Regarding integrated circuits, EMC is becoming an important topic in this domain of the electronic circuitry. There are a lot of reasons for this phenomenon on chip level, such as the more and more complex systems which are integrated, high speed used for digital systems and mixed signal applications. EMC related problems can be found on chip level for the following items: — latch-up in digital circuitry — simultaneous switching noise (substrate) — crosstalk, also for interconnections in MCMs — crosstalk from substrate to bonding wires and pins — decoupling of power supply on chip level — non-linear behaviour of (analog) circuits — mixed analog/digital applications — EMC behaviour of packages In this paper, some of the mentioned phenomena will be discussed in more detail.

articleTitle: A Method for Measuring Free-Space Antenna Factors
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Computer simulations for determining the most appropriate antenna factor to be used in EMI measurements show that the free space antenna factor is much better than the conventional one obtained at a height of 2 or 3m above a ground plane. Further, an improved standard site method for EMI antenna calibration is proposed for determining free-space antenna factors at an open-area test site. Theoretical and experimental analyses show suitable antenna arrangements in detail and confirm that the proposed method yields accurate free-space antenna factors.

articleTitle: Representation of Wide-Band Spectra using an Adaptive, Nonuniform Sampling Scheme
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper discusses a technique for adaptively determining the frequencies for a wide-band CW measurement. Usually, spectral measurements are made with either a linear or logarithmic spacing of frequency sample points, and this results in a poorly sampled spectrum if too few points are chosen. An alternative to this approach is to adaptively locate frequency points in the spectrum, based on an a-priori knowledge of the spectrum. In this way, points can be located at the frequencies where the spectrum is largest and provides the greatest contribution to the transient response. This approach has been successfully adapted to calculations of transient responses using analytically defined spectra. The present paper suggests an extension of this concept to the experimental determination of EM spectral responses.

articleTitle: A Multi-Method Approach to PCB Placement Under EMC and Thermal Constraints
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Placement of components on a PCB under EMC, thermal, geometrical and technological constraints is a highly complex design task which gets more and more important. Especially EMC and thermal constraints require the application of global optimizing methods in order to simultaneously consider all nets. In this paper the new placement tool PLACE-BOX is presented with its concept and selected methods. The tool has been applied to different placement problems and good results in terms of both satisfaction of constraints as well as computation time have been obtained.

articleTitle: How to Decide on the Minimum Number of Frequency Samples to Characterize Linear Networks
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A technique to determine the minimum number of measured frequency samples to characterize the response of a linear network is presented. Then an algorithm to interpolate and extrapolate the measurements is developed. Numerical and preliminary experimental validation is given.

articleTitle: Multi-Stage Models for Modeling EMI Emissions for Complex Problems
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper discusses work that used multiple stage models for real-world problem that was too complex for a single model to effectively simulate the EMI emissions correctly. The output of the first stage model is used as the input for the second stage model, thus allowing each of the modeling stages to be optimized for the problem at hand. Each modeling technique has advantages and disadvantages, and in this case, no one modeling technique could meet the requirements to model this problem. For this problem each modeling stage used different a modeling technique.

articleTitle: One Year After the Coming into Force of EMC Directive: Time to Remove the EMC Components?
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The author of this report is president of the directorate of an international network of EMC engineering companies with EMC test labs located in France, Germany and Switzerland. In this function he is in a good position for drawing up the balance-sheet of the EMC Directive inside and outside the European Union.

articleTitle: Errors Due to the Use of the Transmission Line Model for Calculating Hemp-Induced Currents on Aerial Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper discusses the errors arising from the use of the transmission line theory for computing the currents induced on overhead lines by a high altitude electromagnetic pulse (HEMP) at large distances from the Zero point of the explosion. It is shown that the error in determining the induced current amplitude can be two of factor or higher, and the error in defining the pulse rise time reaches one order of magnitude. It is also shown, that the magnitude of these errors depens on the angle of incidence and conductivity from the ground. It is found the cause for assing these errors.

articleTitle: Analysis of Shielding Characteristics of Ferromagnetic Cable Shields in the Time Domain
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper describes a numerical technique for time-domain analysis of shielding characteristics of ferromagnetic tubular shields taking into account the effects of hysteresis. The frequency dependent Jiles model of ferromagnetic hysteresis and a finite difference technique are used to solve the field distribution inside the ferromagnetic shield in time-domain. Results of three different models of hysteresis are compared for an impulse excitation. The effects of the ferromagnetic hysteresis on the shielding properties are illustrated by several examples.

articleTitle: High Power Electromagnetics
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The High Power Electromagnetics Working Group is one of several working groups that form the basis of the International Union of Radio Science’s Commission E. Background and purpose of the working group are presented. After, a technical example of the requirements for lethality in high power electromagnetics is presented.

articleTitle: Computer-Aided Design of Nonlinear Protection Circuits
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The transient response of multistage protection circuits from overvoltages is investigated both from the theoretical and the experimental points of view. Two simulation tools are proposed which allow to predict the performance of the nonlinear device. The first approach makes use of the common circuit simulator SPICE. SPICE models for gas arresters, varistors and suppressor diodes are presented. The second one is based on an efficient iterative procedure which allows the accurate solution of the timedomain model of the device. Moreover, the frequency-domain analysis of the small-signal equivalent circuit is performed in order to ascertain the linear distorsion produced during the normal operating conditions of the system.

articleTitle: Concepts of Macromodel Libraries
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper describes requirements and tasks becoming obvious in managing macromodels for simulation tools with respect to a widely full-automated analysis-process. A concept regarding the formulated requirements will be presented. Additionally, the interfaces necessary for an useful application of a model-library as part of the analysis-process will be treated. By help of the example of the INCASES Engineering GmbH device library and its integrated interface - both part of the EMC-Work bench a solution will be shown.

articleTitle: Effects of Electromagnetic Interference and Transient Disturbances on Electronic Components and PCBs
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper deals with the activities of the working group E6 within the URSI Commission E. One of its main objective is to investigate new approaches to study the effect of electromagnetic interference on electronic components and PCBs. Additionally, new trends on future measurement standards are outlined.

articleTitle: Theoretical and Experimental Determination of the Shielding Effectiveness of Test Enclosures
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this paper, the shielding effectiveness (SE) of enclosures is characterized experimentally as well as theoretically. First, an accurate measurement set-up is developed, enabling SE measurements in an anechoic chamber, at 3 meters from the DUT (Device Under Test). Secondly, full-wave simulations are performed, thus allowing an accurate comparison between measured and simulated results. A very good correspondence is obtained between experimental and theoretical results, with a discrepancy of less than 5 dB (for frequencies below the first resonance frequency of the enclosure). Also the resonance effects inside the box are efficiently predicted by the simulation tool.

articleTitle: Use of a Helical Coordinate System and Finite Differences to Determine the Charge Densities and Capacitances of a Shielded Twisted Pair Transmission Line
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The surface charge densities and associated capacitances of a shielded twisted pair transmission line are found for quasi static conditions, under balanced and longitudinal excitation. A helical coordinate system is developed in which the potential distribution can be expressed in two dimensions. Laplace's equation is defined in the new coordinate system. The potential distribution throughout the structure is found using a Finite Difference technique on Laplace's equation. The gradient normal to the surface of the conductor is used to find the charge densities on the inner wires and the shield. The model uses exact boundary conditions, and is not limited in the range of physically realizable twist lengths.

articleTitle: Modelling and Simulation of Radiated or Conducted Immunity Tests
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper proposes two simple approaches to model, simulate and predict the electromagnetic radiated or conducted immunity tests on the harness of electronic systems in standard testing situations based on in-situ measurements. In the first approach, the coupling model is determined by recording the voltages at each port of interest in a harness and deducing the equivalent sources to include at each considered port in order to reproduce the same results as far as the loads are concerned. The second part of this paper considers a more general approach using exclusively measured scattering parameters. Comparisons between predictive simulations and in-situ measurements are presented in the case of a simple radiated transmission line and in the case of a 10 port arbitrary wired structure tested by radiation and by current injection.

articleTitle: EMC Education in Italian Universities
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Several EMC courses have been recently established in Italian universities. They are offered to students who attend a five-year "laurea" or a three-year "diploma" course in the engineering school. An overview of these educational EMC courses pursued in Italy is presented.

articleTitle: Earth Potential Distribution Around High-Voltage Substations in Rural and Urban Areas
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The earth potential rise around high-voltage substations in case of faults may cause dangerous voltages between nearby telephone subscriber lines and neutral ground. In rural and urban areas the substation grounding system may be connected to or located near to a large and complex network of conductors composed of metal sheaths of power and telecommunication cables, pipes for water, gas and heating, and rails of traffic systems. Such complex structures may increase the earth potential rise zone of influence. This paper presents analysis of parameters that have dominant influence on the earth potential distribution in urban areas.

articleTitle: Development of an EMC-Constraint PCB Design, Placement and Routing Support Tool
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The EMC-constraint CAD layout support tool was developed for the printed circuit board design. In the developed system two possible constraints; signal reflection and crosstalk, were considered. The former was taken into account in the element placement stage and the latter was considered in the routing stage. At the placement stage reflections were first calculated for all combinations of the parameters. And then the allowable length table was constructed. The constraint to the line length and thus the placement was indicated to the designer in the manual layout stage. The crosstalk was also calculated for all possible combinations of the parameters. These results were stored in the database. The routing constraint are given from the database-table during the manual layout operation. The tool can help the layout designer interactively and visually. In this paper the system configuration of the support tool and its applications are demonstrated. The consideration on the other noise sources are now in progress.

articleTitle: Metalized Flexible Materials and Their Use in Gaskets, Thermoforms and Architectural Shielding
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: For E-field and far-field shielding the thickness of the metal layer required to obtain a given shielding effectiveness is only fractions of micrometers. It is therefore possible to substitute full metal shielding parts with fabrics or non-wovens that are metalized. They are able to provide a sufficient level of attenuation combined with the intrinsic constructial advantages of fabrics and non-wovens such as flexibility, formability, handling and weight reduction. This paper gives an overview of a number of processes used to metalise flexible materials, the different metals that can be applied and the applications of metalized flexible materials in EMI-gaskets, thermoform parts and architectural shielding.

articleTitle: Shielding Materials and Enclosures: Basic Shielding Theory.
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Tackling interference problems may be done at three different levels of a system: — by acting on the source level and reducing the emission level and spectrum. — by acting on the victim level, by reducing the susceptibility (or increasing the immunity) by design. — by acting on the transmission path. This latter action is depending on the coupling path. For conductive problems, the use of filtering techniques must be considered. For radiated problems, the use of shielding techniques is required. Because shielding is directly related to radiation, electromagnetic field theory is concerned with. Therefor, some basic shielding theory is reviewed in this introductory paper.

articleTitle: Site Attenuation Measurements using Shortened Dipole Antennas
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: For quality validation of EMI test sites, site attenuation measurement with shortened dipole antennas is theoretically and experimentally investigated, in particular, for the frequency range of 30 to 80 MHz. 80- MHz half-wave or tuned dipole antennas are proposed to be used in the so-called classical site attenuation measurements. Before studying site attenuation, the antenna factor and impedance of these antennas are computed using the moment method and compared with measurement results, which show a good agreement within 0.3 dB. Then, using the same numerical method, classical site attenuation values are calculated for shortened dipole antennas. These theoretical values are examined and their accuracy verified by performing measurements at four open-field test sites. Thus, a site attenuation measurement method using shortened dipoles can be established by introducing the theoretical values obtained in this paper. It is also concluded that the use of shortened dipole antennas offers better reproducibility in site attenuation measurements than conventional half-wave or tuned dipole antennas.

articleTitle: Calculation of Transients in Nonlinear Systems Consisting of Elements Described by the Frequency Responses
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Many of EMC problems cannot be solved because of the lack of devices mathematical models. It is convenient to use as a linear mathematical model of the device its experimentally obtained frequency responses. They represent the most simple gained information about the devices. The offered method permits to use in the time domain the models, described by the frequency responses. This allows to calculate the transients in the complex systems with nonlinear elements and the elements, which models could be described only by the frequency responses. Other methods of solving of such problems do not permit to take into account simultaneously both experimental frequency responses and nonlinear elements. The estimation of an error of the offered method is presented in the paper. The application of a method is illustrated by the elementary examples and solving a practical problem.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Implementation of the EMC Directive After One Year by a European Competent Body
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In view of a European Competent Body an attempt has been made to summarize the development in the European EMC scenario one year after the implementation of the directive 89/336/EEC. An illustration of current discussion topics amongst EMC experts in the European Association of Competent Bodies is given. Examples of typical Competent Body case studies under article 10.2 are highlighted. Still existing differences within the European frame works regarding standards interpretation, level and quality of accreditation and metrology are described. Managerial, technical as well as economical consequences are discussed in implementing the directive in large, medium and small enterprises. The important role of market enforcement is identified in conjunction with the critical eye of the competition.

articleTitle: A Novel Approach to Open Area Test Sites for Electrically Small Radiators
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Today used open area test sites (OATS’s) have many problems. 3 m, 10 m and 30 m measurements established in different standards can be converted by poor approximations only. The measurement procedure is very slow due to the need to And maximum field intensities in different positions at each frequency. This article describes a new OATS that avoids these problems for electrically small devices under test (DUT’s) by using an antenna configuration known from direction Anders.

articleTitle: Investigation of the Disturbance Fields of Partial Discharges in Elementary High Voltage Setups
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this paper, the relationship between conductor and field-bound electromagnetic interference of partial discharges is investigated for two model setups. Experimental data are given about typical discharge types and their current waveforms. Furthermore, time behaviour of streamer discharges is considered theoretically. The setup is modelled as a finite conductor arrangement for field calculation according to antenna theory. In this model, a double-exponential pulse waveform with time characteristics adapted to measurement serves as current source. Finally, field levels predicted from this simulation are shown and compared with measured interference field spectra caused by streamer discharges.

articleTitle: Computer Aided Prediction of Crosstalk Effects in CMOS Integrated Circuits
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper details a methodology based on the use of Finite-Element-Method software and recursive layout network extraction for building EMC-related design guidelines in order to tolerate the crosstalk phenomena. The report gives first an introduction to crosstalk avoidance methods, details the basic configurations for worst-case coupling analysis and give some illustration of the technique in the case of wire interspacing optimisation for crosstalk constraints. It also details the principles of a capacitance extraction tool to be used in very large deep sub-micron integrated circuits, and techniques for on-chip noise sampling and characterization.

articleTitle: Integration Methodologies for EMC Analysis Tools
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The use of EMC analysis tools has become an accepted part of the design process of high speed printed circuit boards (PCB). Unfortunately most PCB design tool either lack this analysis functionality as integrated software module or, if this functionality is available, it does not offer the same level of functionality rather then standalone analysis applications. This causes the demand for integrated EMC analysis environments as well as for tools to be available integrated within PCB design tools. For these needs a dedicated client-server application has been developed, called the EMC-Server, which enables an integration of EMC tools into various framework environments as well as into PCB design systems.

articleTitle: Rocket Triggered Lightning
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The artificially triggered lightning experiments by launching rockets is effective to understand the physics of lightning. In this paper we propose to concentrate our attention on this subject as an activity of working group E.4.

articleTitle: FE-TD Analysis of Ferromagnetic Shields Against Near Field Sources
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The Finite Element Method is applied to solve the equations describing the field propagation inside ferromagnetic materials with hysteresis, which are often used to shield low-frequency magnetic fields. The method is applied in the time domain and two procedures are presented to solve the stiffness problem represented by Maxwell’s curl nonlinear equations with integrodifferential boundary conditions.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Radiation of Wire Loops Connected to Electrically Large Bodies
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: To minimize the time and the resources for field calculation it is advisable to use the Geometrical Theory of Diffraction (GTD) instead of the Method of Moments (MoM) as often as possible. The paper describes a procedure to analyse wires connected to conducting surfaces by a combination of MoM and GTD without the body’s subdivision into patches. Furthermore the calculation of antennas placed near to diffracting edges are mentioned. To prove the efficiency of the procedure some calculated examples and experimental results are presented.

articleTitle: An Evaluation of the Shielding Effectiveness of Cabinets
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this paper we compare theoretical and experimental methods used in the evaluation of shielding effectiveness with particular emphasis on a metal cabinet with a single aperture. The techniques studied include both susceptibility and emissions measurements, transmission-line modelling simulation and semi-analytical methods. The shielding effectiveness results obtained using each of the above methods are shown along with a discussion of the relative merits and disadvantages of each approach.

articleTitle: A Study of the Effect of Channel Branching on Lightning Radiation
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: We analyze the effect of lightning channel branching on the temporal waveform of the radiated fields of the return stroke. To model the far-field radiation, we consider the modified transmission line (MTL) model for pulse propagation on the channel, with reflection and transmission of the current pulse at each branching point, and back-reflection from ground and channel tips, then accounting for the related contributions to the radiated field. The effect of branching is also isolated, and compared to the effect of tortuosity of an unbranched channel. The effect of the first branch point and ground back-reflection appear as relevant in establishing the field waveform.

articleTitle: A Workflow-Oriented Environment to Support EMC-Adequate System Design
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Efficient system design under EMC-constraint has gained additional importance with the demands for shorter design cycles and faster time-to-market intervals. With many competitors on the market it is of paramount interest to ship a high-qualitiy product as soon as possible. However, as technological and legal constraints require close attention it is no longer sufficient to simply build a system, but to build it according to these constraints. The area of EMC-related design methodologies is concerned with the design of systems which on the one side do not harm other surrounding ones with electromagnetic effects and on the other side guarantee proper functioning. Due to the growing complexity and the increase in system speed these requirements have become much harder to match. An extended approach to cope with an EMC-adequate system design based on a workflow-oriented tool-integration environment will be introduced. A prototype of a specialized design and analysis environment to support the handling of signal integrity effects is discussed.

articleTitle: Full Statistical Analysis of an ESD Environment
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The authors present a direct and complete method for the statistical characterization of an equipment subjected to electrostatic discharges. The approach relies on the knowledge of the transfer function of the system (or something equivalent) which allows one to evaluate the dependence of the relevant output variables on the parameters which can cause a failure. Since these parameters are, in general, randomly variable, their properties are described through suitable probability density functions whose algebraic manipulation and combination allows one to derive the statistical distribution of the output variables as well. The probability of an undesired response then results from an analysis method which takes into account either the sensitivity on the input variables or their occurrence probability. With the aim of giving a practical example, the method is applied with great detail to the particular case of the coupling of an ESD into a shielded enclosure through an aperture. The way for taking into account a variable susceptibility is also highlighted and introduced in the model.

articleTitle: Design-Flow to Support the Simulation, Modelling and Optimization of EMC-Behaviour of Input and Output Stages of CMOS and BICMOS Integrated Circuits
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper deals with the Simulation and Modelling of IC characteristics under EMC constraints. The design flow of system development considering IC properties is illustrated. Methods for the generation of I/O models of integrated circuits, independent of any process technology, as well as package models are explained.

articleTitle: EMC Models and Experimental Measurements Used for Educational Purposes in the Telecommunication Industry
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: An EMC course for designers of telecommunication equipment holds in our company is presented. The course covers signal integrity, EMI/EMC problems regarding ICs, PCBs, cables and racks. The phenomena are explained using experimental data obtained by simple structures. Design rules are given by simple analytical models verified comparing calculated and measured results.

articleTitle: Lightning Electric Field Data Used for the Design of Surge Protective Devices
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Since about 15 years the electric and magnetic fields radiated by lightning were measured in the region of Munich. From these measurements the ratios of the current amplitudes and the current steepness of positive to negative return strokes to ground were derived. It was found that the positive return strokes contain higher current amplitudes as well as higher current steepness than the negative return strokes. For the coordination of surge protective devices the currents with the lowest maximum current steepness and the lowest amplitude have to be considered. Therefore, protecting against negative return strokes the protection against positive return strokes is included in the coordination concept.

articleTitle: Transmission Line Matrix (TLM) Models of Electromagnetic Fields in Space and Time
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper describes principles of, and progress in the modeling of electromagnetic structures in three-dimensional space and time with the Transmission Line Matrix (TLM) method. While this circuit-based technique has now reached a certain level of maturity, research efforts continue to improve its accuracy, speed, user friendliness, flexibility, and its compatibility with tools based on more conventional techniques.

articleTitle: Electrical and EMC Engineering Education: An IEEE United States Perspective
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: For the past twenty years the IEEE EMC-Society has been observing EMC education in U.S. universities and industry and attempting to encourage its growth. This paper offers a personal view by the author on the status of EMC education in U.S. schools and industry and looks at one possible future in each area.

articleTitle: A Model of Positive Lightning Stepped Leader and its Radiated Electromagnetic Fields
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper presents a short description of a simplified model (taking into account some atmospheric conditions) allowing to predict positive lightning discharge characteristics. The model uses an equivalent electrical network, the parameters of which are determined from electromagnetic fields calculation, physical laws and gas discharge theories. A short description of the approach is given with particular attention to the proposed refinements. Procedure is furthermore given to determine the electric and magnetic fields associated to the lightning stepped leader. All the obtained results characteristics are quite satisfactories.

articleTitle: Electrostatic Discharge in Fluid Lines in the Petroleum and Aerospace Industry
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Electrostatic charge generation as a result of fluid flow in pipes has been studied by the scientific community for the past century. A complete mathematical model has not been developed to explain all aspects of the charging process. Cases of Electrostatic Discharge (ESD) causing failures in fluid lines have been around since the early sixties in the petroleum industry. Very few cases of ESD fluid line failures in the Aerospace Industry have been discovered until now.

articleTitle: Fundamentals of the EMC Current Probes
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The basic physical description of the AC or RF current probes is presented and the corresponding equivalent-circuit representation is derived. This information is adequate for a fundamental understanding of the principles of the design and use of this device. The same principles and construction criteria apply to the reversed use of the probe, i. e. to the Bulk-Current-Injection couplers. The main non-ideal aspects of the device behavior are also presented.

articleTitle: Ionospheric Scattering of Broadcast Signals as a Source of Stochastic Interference to Highly Sensitive HF Radio Systems
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: It is shown that the level of HF broadcast signals in shadow zones on the Earth’s surface, provided by wave scattering from small scale ionospheric inhomogeneities often can greatly exceed that of the cosmic background which is generally assumed as the main source of HF noise. Knowledge of the statistics of such signals is therefore very important for the operation of highly sensitive radio systems in the waveband. Statistical characteristics of scattered signals are investigated in the paper both theoretically and experimentally. The highly directional antenna array of the UTR-2 radio telescope was used for observations. The statistical distribution, space and time correlation functions, angular and power spectra and total power of the scattered signals are discussed.

articleTitle: Shielding Materials and Enclosures: Shielding Measuring Methods.
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Specifying shielding materials in modern electronic system design is a rather complicated decision to make. The influence of a lot of effects has to be taken into account: holes, openings, joints, etc. Therefor, the choice of a shielding material will depend on a series of requirements, also for mechanical design. The Shielding Effectiveness (SE) of a material may be specified using different methods. These methods are used for the evaluation of materials under both near field and far field conditions. All these methods have advantages and disadvantages, ranging from carefull sample preparation up to very time consuming measurements in order to obtain exact SE-values. In this paper, an overview will be given of a lot of measuring methods and procedures for the evaluation of the shielding effectiveness under different conditions and applications. Three typical families of measurements are discussed: — SE characterisation of shielding materials. Flat samples are used for this purpose. — SE characterisation of holes, slots, joints and gaskets. — SE characterisation of shielding enclosures and rooms (architectural shielding).

articleTitle: Improvement of Design Process for Development of High Speed Digital Printed Circuit Boards
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Early implementation of signal integrity and EMC design considerations and constraints in the design flow can significantly improve the reliability of any system and reduce the necessity of redesigns after first prototyping. The influence of different parameters on simulation results are discussed and three tested ways for simulation methodology are presented. An essential point for the successful installation of simulation strategies is the availability of accurate behavioural models of the input/output buffers from IC vendors.

articleTitle: Analysis of Field Coupling to Nonuniform Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this paper we study the responses of finite-length nonuniform and uniform transmission lines (TLs) excited by an incident electromagnetic wave. Externally excited uniform TLs have closed-form solutions in terms of inverse chain matrix, whereas nonuniform TLs cannot be analytically solved. Here, we adopt the concept of cascaded line as the method of solving this latter situation. To confirm the validity of this method, theoretical and experimental results of coupling calculations for a few typical line geometries are presented.

articleTitle: Transient Response of a Thin Wire in a Two-Media Configuration
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The transient response of a thin wire radiating in the presence of an inhomogeneous medium is obtained by solving the corresponding time-domain integral equation of the Hallen type. A new mathematical model proposed in this paper is based on the extension of the free space Hallen equation utilizing the space-time dependent Fresnel reflection coefficient. The space-time current distribution along the antenna or the scatterer is obtained by the originally developed finite element integral equation method (FEIEM) applying the Galerkin-Bubnov procedure.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Effects of Cellular Radiotelephone on Motor Vehicles and Their Standards
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Today, a lot of numeric modelling studies are carried out in the car industry to determine the electromagnetic condition in the vehicle. The purpose of these studies is to determine the car passenger cell effects on the coupling level and mode of electromagnetic disturbances. The passenger cell is an enclosed environment, pratically a Faraday cage, which an anechoic chamber test does not simulate properly. The present state of motor vehicle standards reflect this problem, since bench tests (ISO 11452) and complete motor vehicle tests (ISO 11451) are different. The study presented here deals with the correlation problem between anechoic chamber and passenger cell car testing for the particular case of cellular radiotelephone electromagnetic disturbances. Considering the increased use of this communication tool, for which one of the main uses is in cars, cellular radiotelephone disturbances have to be differentiated by a specific motor vehicle test. Now, the present ENV 50204 standard (immunity to electromagnetic field generated by numeric radiotelephone) does not take into account this specificity. Similarly, the complete motor vehicle test ISO 11451 does not take into account the cellular radiotelephone disturbances specificity. There is therefore a problem to which the present study tries to answer with an easy experimental simulation. Many practical results of coupled current and voltage to a test D.U.T. (Device Under Test), and taking into account the interaction cellular radiotelephone antenna/ D.U.T., are given for different bench and car test configurations. The electric field generated near the cellular radiotelephone antenna is also measured. Finally, a synthesis allows to give a first answer concerning the correlation between present standards (ENV 50204 / ISO 11451) and the particular cellular radiotelephone disturbances in the motor vehicle environment.

articleTitle: One Year Experience with the Market Surveillance in Germany and the System Developed for that Goal
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The provisions concerning the testing of equipment on the market which have to be complied with in Germany are not only based on the EMVG (German EMC Act) but also on the Telecommunication Act (TKG) which transposed the Terminal Directive 91/263/EEC into national law. Both laws are applicable in this context since the provisions of the EMVG and of the Terminal Directive are closely related when the equipment is tested on the premises of the customer. During the transitionary period until December 31, 1995, different types of marking of the equipment, type-examination certificates, certificates of conformity and provisions of the European Community may be applied in Germany. The large number of requests received and the experience gathered whithin the framework of the testing of equipment on the market have releaved that many manufacturers and import companies are not yet familiar with the relevant laws and regulations. Thus, the activities of market observation will focus on providing information to the parties concerned, following the general principle: explanation rather than penalties.

articleTitle: The New National Standard of EM Field Strength; Realization and Dissemination
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: We introduce a new system for generating electromagnetic standard fields in the frequency range up to 1 GHz. It serves now as a national standard for electric field strength at PTB with an uncertainty of < 5 % and consists of 1. a μΤΕΜ-cell with homogeneous field distribution in a usable (test) volume of 16 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, including additional equipment (rf-source, power amplifier, attenuators, and 50-Ω-load) traced to basic Si-units via a calibrated directional coupler, attenuator, rf-power meter, and ac/dc power transfer; 2. a small size sensor (1 cm dia., h: 1.5 mm) for dissemination (transfer) of the electric field strength into larger field generators as working standards, and 3. a GTEM-cell (usable volume ≈0.5 m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>) as internal working standard for EMC tests or calibration of external (reference) field sensors.

articleTitle: Voltage Induced on a Line by a Nearby Lightning Stroke With a Tortuous Channel
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper presents a coupling model between lightning induced field and a transmission line, valid also close to the lightning striking point. Local analytical approximate forms of the incident near field are used to find an analytical-based expression for the induced current or voltage at both ends of the line. The incident field is evaluated starting from a tortuous lightning discharge and employing the so-called modified transmission line (MTL) return stroke model. Comparisons with measured fields and induced voltages show that the tortuous channel model yields simulated electric fields quite similar to those measured in experimental research, and the related induced voltages on the line compare equally well with measurements, both in the far and near regions.

articleTitle: Identification of Disturbances in Cathode-Ray-Tube Monitors.
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Disturbances of monitors and different means to reduce those effects are discussed. Cathode-ray-tubes (widely used in computer, monitors or TV. sets) are already influenced by relatively low magnetic fieldstrengths. Low frequency magnetic fields cause the electron beam to "shake", the characters and figures show a varying deflection. A gradient in a permanent static magnetic field in a room, e.g. the magnetic field of the earth, can cause colour changes and picture distortions on the monitor screen. Also shield current on the data-cable between the monitor and the CPU is a disturbance cause, that makes working with monitors tiresome. If the cable shield is grounded on both cable ends, it is possible that a circuit loop is created. There might circulate an inductively or galvanically coupled current in this loop. Depending on the frequency content of this current the brilliance of the monitor-screen varies its intensity, causing a glittering effect on the screen. The report shows that monitor-picture appearances can considerably be improved by using an appropriate data connection from the monitor to the CPU.

articleTitle: Radiated Emission Measurements in GTEM Cells Compared with Those of an OATS
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The GTEM cell is a broadband transversal electromagnetic waveguide working up to 1 GHz. It is an emerging alternative to open area test site (OATS) measurements. The OATS is the standard environment for emission measurements. Thus the GTEM cell data have to be correlated to the OATS results. This paper describes two methods of performing this correlation and investigates their performance. Measurements in a GTEM cell and on an OATS have been taken and the results have been compared. Special attention is given to the optimal coupling of the equipment under test (EUT) in the cell as poor coupling may lead to lower results than expected.

articleTitle: A Method for Determining the Transmission Direction of Common-Mode Electromagnetic Noise by Measuring its Energy Flow
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Measuring the transmission direction of interference is an effective way to search for interference sources. A method of determining the direction of interference by simultaneously measuring the voltage and current is developed. The method is based on network theory and Fourier analysis. The measurement system which is based on these theories consists of an analog to digital converter and a digital signal processor. A new clamp-type voltage probe with an electrostatic shield is also developed to measure the interference voltage without cutting the cable. Experimental results show that the transmission direction of sinusoidal waves, non-sinusoidal periodic waves and transient waves can be obtained using this system.

articleTitle: Computer Simulation of ESD
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The highly non linear process of ESD of bodies of revolution with perfectly conducting and resistive surface is modeled. Computer simulation is done using an electrodynamic method based on the method of moments (MoM) in time domain. Arc currents, transient fields in near and far zones are calculated and compared with experimental data. As an example of EMC applications, the coupling of transient fields radiated by ESD into a digital circuit is modeled.

articleTitle: Coupling of a Lightning Wave to the Internal Wiring System of a Faraday Shield
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper presents work to be used for drafting a normative document for defining the tests of land-based military equipment exposed to proximity electromagnetic radiation. These indirect effects, due to electromagnetic coupling with antennas, wiring systems and circuits, induce interference, overvoltages and overcurrents (localized aggression) which in turn cause disturbances or damage to the equipment (malfunction, signal transmission errors, destruction of components, loss of functions, etc.). This paper presents the numerical simulations and the validation tests conducted on a shelter exposed to this aggression. The tests were conducted at the Centre d'Essais Aéronautique de Toulouse (CEAT) from 25 March to 3 April 1996 (photo 1).

articleTitle: Using the Moment Method for Modelling the Electromagnetic Field Radiated by Static Converters
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: During the last decade, great achievements in the field of power electronics have significantly contributed to its promotion in all areas of engineering. However, its evolution to an indispensable factor in today's industrial applications has also involved a certain number of problems which have not yet been studied thoroughly or completely solved. These problems are related to electromagnetic compatibility, especially, related to radiated electromagnetic field from circuits of static converters. In this paper, the problem is described by an electric integral equation in terms of the unknown current densities. The solution of this equation is achieved by the moments method. The aim of this paper is to explain how we apply this resolution to circuits of static converters. In fact, printed circuit boards, linear components, nonlinear components, and ground plane are taken into account. For nonlinearity we use a circuit simulator (working in time domain). Numerical results concerning the radiated electric field by a circuit of a chopper are presented and then compared to measurements realised in our laboratory.

articleTitle: The Simulation of the DC-Offset Shift of an OpAMP Due to Crosstalk on PCB-Traces, using a Macro-Model.
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this paper, a modified macro-model for an OpAmp is presented, for the simulation of the DC-offset shift, due to crosstalk on nearby PCB-traces. The model has been developped based on the common known Alexander & Bowers model. 1’he model has been validated for a 741 OpAmp. Both the measured and simulated results, and the Spice listing of the model are presented.

articleTitle: Developments in Emission and Immunity Testing
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper will review recent trends in making radiated and conducted emission and immunity measurements. Alternate radiated emission measurement will be especially covered in this session and the results compared with measurements made using common test facilities such as open area test sites (OATS) and absorber lined test chambers. These alternate techniques include: a) measuring emissions using monopole antennas, b) predicting radiated emissions based on numerical simulation of the radiating source, c) estimating radiated emissions by first measuring the magnetic near-field of the source, and d) using current probes to predict radiated emissions based on currents on cables attached to equipment under test. For radiated immunity tests, alternates investigated in this session include: a) a new procedure for calibrating the test field, b) the use of a reverberating chamber from a theoretical perspective and c) the use of a reverberating chamber to test for both the radiated emissions and immunity of an entire automotive vehicle. Finally, reference will be made to the present international standards which are most applied for both emission and immunity measurements. In particular, the generic standards as specified in CENELEC will be described, especially since those on emissions are now approved as IEC standards [1,2].

articleTitle: Experiences of a Competent Body With One Year EMC Directive
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The following paper describes the experience of a Competent Body working with the EMC Directive and gives an overview of the situations and problems Competent Bodies have been facing in the past year. Not all these problems are related to actual work as Competent Body, but a Competent Body is often consulted by manufacturers requesting information or help in related area’s. Furthermore the CB’s have gathered knowhow related to a large variety of products to be tested.

articleTitle: EMC - Education at the Fachhochschule Mannheim
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: EMC - basis training in the Institute for High Voltage Technology. Emphasis lies on the experimental treatment of impulse - and linebound disturbances.

articleTitle: A New Methodology for Direct Modeling of Radiation Coupling to Interconnects using SPICE
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A new methodology for the modeling of multiconductor transmission lines with distributed sources in SPICE is presented. The new model is based on the use of Chebyshev polynomials for the representation of the spatial variation of the voltages, currents and distributed sources along the transmission line. A simple collocation procedure is used to obtain a matrix representation of the approximated generalized telegrapher’s equations with matrix coefficients that are first polynomials in the Laplace transform variable s. The time-dependent form of this matrix representation is compatible with the modified nodal analysis formalism, and its implementation in SPICE is straightforward. With this new formulation, coupling of electromagnetic radiation of arbitrary temporal and spatial variation to interconnects with position-dependent per-unit-length parameters can be modeled efficiently in SPICE. Numerical examples are presented to demonstrate the validity of the proposed model.

articleTitle: Measurement Error and Field Distortion of Magnetic Field Sensors
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The measurement error of magnetic field probes and their properties are investigated by a computer program for numerical field calculation based on the method of moments. The simulation of the different sensor types and the variation of their probe characteristics have shown which factors have an influence on the deviation from the true field. The definition of a relative deviation enables comparison of the sensors in different field distributions. The results are verified by analytical calculations and measured examples.

articleTitle: Space Structure of Magnetic Field Component for Geometrically Different Types of Lightning
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The expressions for calculation of different return stroke field components are given. They are submitted in form widely used in lightning’s calculation practice. The basic element for field calculations is the straight line channel situated in a free space. In the frame of infinite conductive ground it is possible to calculate and examine fields from more complicated lightning channels (inclined, tortuous, brandling). Some examples for space waveform variations for several simple lightning models with one-segment (vertical, inclined, horizontal ) and three-segments channel are discussed. The special attention is called to the fact that the variable limits of integrating in the expressions given differ from ones used in ordinary field calculation practice. Besides limits for the primary and mirror (reflected from the ground) sources can be differ from each other too for arbitrary situated observation point (excluding the case when it situated on the ground level). All examples discussed are given for the fixed distance 50km in order to exclude the waveform variations caused by distance changing. Besides for this distance (and more) it is possible to use the term “directional diagram” for describing of space distribution of signals amplitudes.

articleTitle: Fast Time Domain Simulation of Reflection and Crosstalk Noise on Lossy Interconnects
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this paper a fast time domain simulation technique for the analysis of reflection and crosstalk noise on lossy transmission lines is presented. The approach is based on modelling an area of homogenious transmission lines by the model of delayed current components which can be integrated very easily into existing analogue circuit simulators. Significant quantities of this model are the current transfer matrix and the characteristic admittance matrix, which are in general frequency dependent, even if the primary transmission line parameters are assumed to be independent of the frequency. For transient simulations these quantities are required in time domain. As their frequency dependence is not given explicitely, analytical methods cannot be applied directly to perform the required transfomation from frequency to time domain. Using the Padé approximation the elements of these matrices are represented by appropriate fractions of polynomials, which can be transformed easily into time domain after their expansion into partial fractions. The results are sums of weigthed and delayed dirac impulses und exponential functions which are appropriate for a recursive convolution procedure in order to speed up the computaion time significantly. In particular, using the recursive convolution the computation time increases solely linear with the simulation time, where this dependence is of quadratic order in case of the ordinary discrete convolution. The approach is examinated with real life transmission line configurations. Numerical results are compared with those of other existing methods.

articleTitle: Ray-Optical Chaos in Mode-Stirred Reverberating Enclosures
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A simple, ray-optical model of mode-stirred reverberating enclosures, exhibits all relevant features in terms of chaos. The chaotic transition occurs as the peak-to-peak harmonic wall displacement becomes comparable to the EM wavelength. Reverberating properties can be related to and described in terms of Lyapounov exponents. Simple design optimization criteria emerge quite naturally.

articleTitle: Steps Taken to Determine why Different IEC 1000-4-2 ESD Simulators Produce Different Results
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Two different types (manufacturers) of Electro-Static Discharge (ESD) simulators were used in the verification of two different products. In one case the product passed with simulator A and failed with simulator B [2,4], The other product failed with simulator A and passed with simulator B [2]. Similar results were reported by Pommerenke [3,5] Both ESD simulators complied with the IEC 1000-4-2 contact discharge pulse requirements when tested with the defined target and a 1 GHz scope. The information presented herein is intended to improve the knowledge of ESD events with the goal of improving the accuracy and repeatability of ESD testing. Better simulators can only be made if the element to be simulated is more precisely defined. The data shows the variability of current ESD simulators when measured with ultrafast high voltage test equipment and wide band test accessories developed to identify why ESD simulators produce different results depending on product sensitivities.

articleTitle: A New Transmission Line Device With Double Polarization Capability for Use in Radiated EMC Tests
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The subject of this paper is the design and performance analysis of a double polarization transmission line device for radiated EMC tests, the CrossTEM (X-TEM) cell. The X-TEM cell is a multi-wire transmission line device which has been specifically designed in order to optimize the test region dimensions while ensuring double polarization performance and suitable cross polarization level. The most original features found are a particular design of the transmission line septum, which ensures an efficient field generation together with a considerable improvement in the impedance control of the transmission line. Theoretical results illustrating the main improvements obtained are shown, and compared with other solutions already presented in the literature.

articleTitle: Comments on the Significance of Retardation Effects in Calculating the Radiated Electromagnetic Fields from an Extending Discharge
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A cloud-to-ground lightning return-stroke channel is usually modeled as an extending line with one end fixed at ground. Return-stroke models describe how the current is varying with time along the line. The expressions for electric and magnetic fields due to retarded currents on a stationary straight wire antenna of fixed length have been derived in time domain previously (e.g., [1]). These general integral expressions can be used in lightning field calculations with suitable modifications to take into account retarded channel length and possible current discontinuity at the discharge front. The radiation fields far from the channel are generally expressed in terms of the time derivative of the retarded channel current. For the Transmission Line (TL) model which is characterized by a current wave moving vertically without distortion or attenuation at the same speed and in the same direction as the discharge front, the radiation fields observed at ground level very far from the channel are directly proportional to the channel current multiplied by the propagation speed v, as shown, for instance, by [2], However, as demonstrated in [3] and [4], for the case of a channel that is arbitrarily oriented with respect to the observer's line of sight the field/current expressions noted above are in need of correction. A similar correction was also found to be needed in the field/current expressions for a travelling current discontinuity [5], Both corrections are due to retardation effects and appear as a multiplier [1-(v/c)cosθ0]<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>, where c is the speed of light, and θ is the angle between the direction of propagation of the current and the line joining the source and the field point, to the original equations. In this paper we (1) discuss the various situations in which the above factor can arise, (2) give physical interpretation of this factor, and (3) show that the retardation effects in calculating lightning radiation fields can be accounted for without the explicit use of the above factor.

articleTitle: ISO Open Meeting on the International Space Systems EMC Standard
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
