abstract: An international standard is needed to ensure compatibility on space systems. The Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC) Requirements, Space Systems standard is being developed by NASA with international participation to achieve a value added cost effective standard that addressees all necessary EMC areas. This paper describes the history, organization, description, development and plans for the International Standards Organization (ISO) EMC Requirements, Space Systems Standard.

articleTitle: Bipolar Electric Field Pulses in Lightning Flashes Over Sweden
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Bipolar electric field pulse trains associated with cloud-to-ground (CG) lightning flashes and cloud flashes in Sweden are analysed. The bipolar pulse train in negative CG flashes preceded the first return stroke on average by 26 ms and had an average duration of less than 2 ms. These pulses have an initial positive (atmospheric electricity sign convention) polarity, the same polarity as the succeeding return stroke. The bipolar pulse train preceding the return stroke in a positive CG flash has generally two distinct regions. The first region contained bipolar pulses with positive initial polarity and the second region contained bipolar pulses with negative initial polarity, the same polarity as the succeeding positive return stroke. These pulse trains preceded the positive return stroke on average by 60 ms, more than twice the time interval between the bipolar pulse train and the succeeding return stroke in negative CG flashes. The bipolar pulse train in cloud flashes began with the static field change and had an average duration of 13 ms, much longer than bipolar pulse trains in ground flashes. The individual bipolar pulse characteristics and the interval between pulses were very similar in negative and positive CG flashes, however, the bipolar pulses in cloud flashes were wider and more separated from each other.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Coupling to Cables With Shield Interruptions
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The presence of connectors or other shield interruptions can seriously degrade the EMI protection provided by the braid of an otherwise well-shielded cable system. The paper presents a methodology to determine the internal response of a discontinuous shielded cable to an exciting electromagnetic field. The analysis is performed considering different types of discontinuities such as cable connectors, pigtail terminations, and interrupted shield. For the specific case of a cable with the shield interrupted at the middle, the theoretical results have been compared with experimental data obtained using a bounded wave EMP simulator.

articleTitle: Accuracy and Stability Advancements of the Partial Element Equivalent Circuit Model
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The Partial Element Equivalent Circuit (PEEC) technique is a circuit based formulation which is numerically equivalent to a full wave method of moments solution with Galerkin matching. In this paper, advancements are made to the PEEC model through the development of a refined method of computing both the partial inductances as well as the coefficients of potential without increasing the number of unknowns. In addition, damping is added to the PEEC model in order to further reduce unwanted resonances outside the normal frequency range. The effectiveness of the method is illustrated with several examples. Also, we compare our results with a conventional Method of Moments (MoM) code.

articleTitle: Uncertainty of the Frequency Spectra Produced by a Reference Radiator
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper describes a program of measurements to determine the measurement uncertainty associated with the reference radiator. It discusses how these measurements are made and their results. It shows a sample of the frequency spectra produced by the reference radiator, and gives sample calculations for applying its uncertainty to typical EMC measurements in which it is used. For substitution measurements, the amplitude uncertainty of its frequency spectra is equal to or less than 0.06 dB, and the frequency uncertainty is less than 0.18%. As an absolute source, it can be calibrated with an expanded uncertainty of 1.32 dB or less.

articleTitle: Response of Swtiched-Mode Power Supplies to Fast Transient Conducted Disturbances
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: PSPICE-models of the three fundamental components of a switched-mode power supply unit: power-line filter, over-voltage protection element with non-linear impedance-characteristic and switched-mode converter are discussed. Simulation and experimental validation of the common-mode transient response of a typical switched-mode power supply unit is also presented. These models afford an electronic designer or engineer the possibility of simulating the effectiveness of his designs with regard to commonmode transient response without having to invest funds and time in building prototypes of the proposed device.

articleTitle: Field Sensor With Optical Conversion and Link
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In many cases of EMC measurements the field strength interacts with the sensor and the test object. Mainly metallic peaces like cases and leads generate these measurement fealsures. In this contribution an isotropic interference free E-field sensor will be described having not these disadvantages. Basing on new technologies this prototype of sensor consists of 9 cm thin film resistive dipoles positioned in 3 orthogonal axes. A low threshold 1550 nm laser diode is placed in the middle of every dipole to convert the induced field strength values into optical data. Via optical links 3 optical receivers combine the vector sum of correct amplitude and phase values. The energy for the 3 laser diode modulators is generated in a special optical power pack positioned at the rear of every dipole. The power pack contains 12 selective photo diodes which are illuminated by external remote controlled high intensity laser light of 800 nm. This new field sensor is free from interactions with metallic devices and provides correct amplitude and phase informations of the measured fields. So conventionalEMC receivers can be connected for EMC testing.

articleTitle: On the Use of the Laplace Equation to Analyze Low-Frequency Shielding Problems
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A nodal-based finite element method (FEM) is presented to analyze low frequency magnetic fields inside and outside shielded enclosures. The method is able to solve numerically time-harmonic fields in terms of magnetic scalar potential in the source-free, nonconductive region, while the field penetration inside non-perfectly conductive shield regions is analytically solved by transmission line equations. Imposing adequate constrained boundary conditions on the shield surfaces, the shielding problem is solved by the FEM analysis of the Laplace equation in the non-conductive region. The proposed method is suitable to take into account both flux leakage and field penetration.

articleTitle: A Time-Domain Model for Computing the Response of Multiconductor Transmission Line Networks
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this paper, we describe a time-domain technique to calculate the induced currents and voltages on multiconductor transmission line (MTL) networks, which contain resistive circuits in the junctions. The network can be excited by an external plane wave or by voltage sources which are located at any circuit of the system. The method is based on a time-space centered finite-difference technique to solve the time-domain MTL coupled equations. This approach makes it possible to solve a linear matrix system which can be expressed under the AX=B form, where the vector X contains the unknowns of the problem. In the case of a MTL containing at least one shielded cable, the analysis can be based on a global approach with the reference plane on the ground surface, or with multiple references (ground surface and shield). The equivalence with the classical two step method is shown.

articleTitle: Application of a Circuit-Based Approach to Ensuring the Stability of Modified Finite Difference Time-Domain Algorithms.
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: One disadvantage of FDTD is the computational overhead incurred in analysing electrically small details - in EMC for example, wires and slots are of interest. This problem may be overcome by including a priori knowledge of the field’s behaviour in the algorithm however this frequently causes instability. Recently the authors have presented a circuit-based technique for ensuring stability of FDTD methods - this contribution provides full and previously unpublished details of this technique. The method is used to produce a stable formulation incorporating knowledge of the narrow slot static field solution and results obtained for an EMC problem are presented.

articleTitle: Test Facilities
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This session considers EMC test facilities for radiated immunity and emission measurements. A driving force in test facility development is to reduce the expense of EMC product testing. Thus, less costly facilities and reduced measurement times are sought. This session will consider various test facilities and methods to advance the above goals.

articleTitle: Results of the Simultaneous Lightning Current and Lemp-Measurements at the Peissenberg
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper presents the lightning current and T.F.MP data measured at the telecomunication tower on the mountain "Hoher Peissenberg". A statistical evaluation of the long continuing currents as well as of the impulse currents an the LEMP is given. The long continuing currents are evaluated by the charge they contain. The statistical outcome for the charge is shown for the total of measurements and distinguished between lightning through the summer months and lightning through the winter months. Concerning the impulse currents and the LEMP data the paper presents the statistical outcome of the front shape parameters. Finally a new aspect of the impulse currents following to the continuing current is shown.

articleTitle: Present and Future Status of EMC in Brazil and South America
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Brazilian history and status on EMC Regulations are provided. The private and governmental organizations related to the matter are introduced. The relationship between the Brazilian and South-American Normalization (focusing MERCOSUL) is briefed. At the end, an explanation of expected progress to the near future is outlined.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Method Based on the Multiconductor Transmission Line Equation and the Method of Moments
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A hybrid method which combines the Method of Moments (MoM) and the multiconductor transmission line (MTL) equations is presented in this paper. The MTL-equations are used to calculate the current distribution on signal traces and cables. Via the MoM the behaviour of scattering objects (conduction plates, boxes, screens, etc.) is described. The coupling between structures described by the two methods can be taken into account with the help of an integral equation for the electrical field strength and an iterative algorithm. The method will be examined with real life configurations.

articleTitle: Comparison of EMC Measurements in Time and Frequency Domain by Automotive Examples
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The subject of the paper is the comparison between EMC measurements in frequency and time domain. Especially the automotive industry and it's suppliers were forced to decrease their costs in the last years. To reduce the costs of EMC measurements, it is discussed whether time domain techniques can help to save money. Time domain measurements are often faster and therefore a replacement or supplement of frequency domain measurement by time domain techniques leads to an essential economic advantage.

articleTitle: EMC Modelling: From IC to System
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this paper we give an overview of a hierarchical approach to predict the EMC behaviour of an electronic system based on the EMC characteristics of the components ( IC’s and PCB’s).

articleTitle: New Aspects of Ferrite Tile Absorber Optimization and Corresponding Measurements
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A multi-layer calculation method based on an extended transmission line model is presented for ferrite absorber optimization purposes. Deduced from this method, it is proved that a thin double-layer has the same reflection effect as one layer with averaged material parameters, also considering each layer thickness (double-layer concept). Furthermore, a new multi-layer measurement method is offered which makes use of the common-mode excitation of a stripline applicator for flexible and calibrated return loss and material properties’ measurements. Both features were applied for analyzing and optimizing a ferrite tile absorber. As reference, measurements in a GTEM cell were carried out.

articleTitle: Analysis and Optimisation of Hybrid Absorbers in Order to Improve the Quality of Anechoic Chambers
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: There are uniform standards for anechoic chambers in the EC since 01.01.1996. The most substantial points are more severe than the previous regulations that were effective in most countries. These strong requirements can only be fulfilled by carefully planning the anechoic chambers with efficient absorbers. The combination of ferrite and foam absorbers is expected to offer the best absorption over a large frequency range. However the components of such hybrid absorbers have to be fitted to each other. The problems involved in the combination of both absorber types are explained in this paper and a procedure that allows an optimisation of hybrid absorbers in a simple way is shown.

articleTitle: Numerical Modeling for EMC
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper is an introduction to the session on Numerical Modeling for EMC at the 1997 Zurich EMC Symposium. It summarizes the important aspects of the papers to be presented and then presents thoughts on how numerical analysis tools and computer simulations can be used to more adequately understand electrically complex systems.

articleTitle: The EMC Directive: A Manufacturer's Perspective
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper outlines a manufacturer’s experience of the EMC Directive from its draft consultation stage, through its publication in the Official Journal, its transition period, and finally during its first year as a mandatory requirement. An outline is presented of the evolution of this manufacturer’s approach to compliance and the assessment of conformity. Some of the encountered difficulties are discussed and some solutions suggested. The paper concludes by looking to the immediate future and offering advice on how manufacturers might become more proactive in their approach.

articleTitle: The Use of Computer Modelling Software for Analysing EMC Shieding
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The use of computer modelling is becoming widespread in many areas of electrical engineering. It is now commonplace in modelling electromagnetic fields at low frequencies and statics. In many cases, software is also available for high frequency modelling, and promises to become even more so. This session covers some of the techniques used in computer modelling, aimed at EMC applications, and in particular the modelling of shielding problems. The full session will expand on many of these topics, to give an insight into some of the techniques currently available for EMC modelling.

articleTitle: Activity of URSI Commission E Working Group: E-7 on Extraterrestrial and Terrestrial Meteorologico Coelectric Environment With Noise and Chaos
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This anide reviews tine progress made recently by UR.S1 Working Group E-7 (Chairman: H. Kikuchi; Co-Chairman: S.S. Moiseev) on Extraterrestrial and Terrestri Meteorologico-Electric Environment with Noise and Chaos. The topics covered are: cosmic dusty plasmas; laboratory dusty plasmas; EHD and EMHD; sell-organization and chaos; terrestrial lightning; planetary lightning; nebular lightning; ball lightning; terrestrial (ionospheric and magnetospheric) noise; extraterrestrial and cosmic noise.

articleTitle: Time-Domain Study of Lossy Multiconductor Transmission Lines With Nonlinear Loads
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this paper, we present our resolution method of Multiconductor Transmission Lines (MTL) problem. The MTL can be aerial conductors, or even printed circuits, and the equivalent sources due to external fields are incorporated. The coupling of conductors induces voltage falls at the electronic device inputs and may involve damage. We also take into account the skin-effect, specially for circuits performing at high frequencies. To deal with this problem, we use the Finite Difference Time-Domain (FDTD) method, considering only exact formulae for ground and conductor resistances. The proposed model permits to simulate any load with a good stability. The calculation time is relatively reduced: currents and voltages are determined by a matrix resolution and we propose resistance formulae which are numerically usable. We apply this method to configurations already treated and our exact formulae allow us to find some differences with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1 /\sqrt{f}$</tex> skin-effect version.

articleTitle: Modelling of the Current Distribution Generated by a Direct Lightning Stroke in a Low-Voltage Installation
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Surge Protective Devices (SPDs) are classified into lightning current arresters, arresters and suppressers. They must be coordinated taking into account their maximum surge current capacities, the medium-to-low voltage transformer, the earth electrode impedance, an eventual domestic charge, and neighbouring residences building. The purpose of this study is to determine the current distribution, in time domain, and the stress on the various SPD in terms of current or energy, induced by a direct lightning stroke on the protector or an overhead line. For this aim, we propose a new analytic formulation for the experimental current, obtained from triggered lightnings. Numerical simulations are made by using E.M.T.P (ElectroMagnetic Transients Program ). We had to use usual models (varistors, earthing) and to propose some others (lightning rod, transformer, waterpipes a consumer equipment...), in order to represent the electric properties of a medium-to-low voltage network.

articleTitle: Lines With Earth Return Inside a Tunnel
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper presents a model for the study of lines with earth return inside a tunnel; the main point is the current density field evaluation inside the tunnel walls; this can be done by solving the non homogeneous Fredholm integral equation on which the model is based; such an equation is solved in a numerical way by means of the moment methods. Finally, some examples of application to a semicircular tunnel together with the tunnel screening effect evaluation are given.

articleTitle: Analysis of RF Injection Effects on Analog Circuits using Harmonic Balance Simulation
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: RF noise immunity is becoming a serious problem for ICs. We have found a frequency domain simulator (Harmonic Balance; HB) to be useful for analyzing undesired IC behavior, especially DC output shift, under the RF injection. The simulator has the following advantages in comparison with a conventional time domain simulator such as SPICE: 1) DC output shifts can be simulated in a very short time, and 2)A steady-state current or voltage waveforms at each node in an IC are directly and easily obtained. This paper describes the methods and results of undesired behavior analysis of a bipolar transistor or a differential amplifier using HB.

articleTitle: Damping Transmission-Line and Cavity Resonances
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In the interaction of electromagnetic fields with complex electronic systems there are often low-loss resonances associated with conductors (transmission-line modes) and cavities. These resonances can allow the effective transmission of undesirable signals through the systems at the resonance frequencies. This paper discusses techniques for suppressing (damping) such resonances. These involve various spatial distributions of resistors (in some cases with inductors (chokes)).

articleTitle: Whole-Vehicle EMC Testing in a Reverberation Chamber
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper presents the results of an experimental program to study the use of reverberation chambers to test whole vehicles for EMC. This program is part of the development of two new SAE standards for land-vehicle EMC testing. The results of this program imply that the test method works and is efficient. However, more study is needed to determine the realism of this testing and to define the comparison between reverberation chamber test results and the results of other methods, e g., SAE J551 [1] or CISPR 12 [2]

articleTitle: Metal Cabinets for EMI Shielding
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper sets out to deal with screen damping measurements of empty enclosures. Evaluation of the measurement results can be by means of a simple method which is introduced by means of a theoretic derivation.

articleTitle: EMI - Modelling of PCB With Respect to System Design
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The simulation of radiation problems of complex Printed Circuit Boards (PCB’s) and of systems at all and with reasonable computing effort (time and resources) is possible only by using of macromodels - simplified but sufficiently accurate models - of certain system parts. Such a macromodel for line systems on PCB’s (e.g. bus systems) suitable for radiation simulations at EMC standard measurement distances is presented. Analyses have proved that the model has a good accuracy and reduces the computing time essentially. With the same computing effort more complex simulation problems can so be solved. The used modelling method is useful also for other macromodelling problems.

articleTitle: Comparison of the RF Immunity of Operational Amplifiers
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A comprehensive series of measurements of RF detection in operational amplifiers of different technologies, manufacturers and production series have been made. It is shown that for RF voltages less than 2 Vrms, the properties of an OP-Amp can be described by a Taylor expansion where the coefficient of the second order term is the dominant parameter. This parameter is shown to be very much dependent on the production technology used (14-20 dB). The dependency on manufacturers of the same type designation is less but significant (3-6 dB). Production data and spread in individuals has almost no influence on detection properties (<1 dB).

articleTitle: Advanced Methods for System Design Under EMC Constraints
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: System design under EMC constraints means to consider EMC-behaviour at system level during all stages of a development process. This requires the introduction of a generalized development process in which the so-called EMC-optimization is integrated. Especially the development of a system from the specification stage to the validation stage will be shown. An EMC knowledge-based system SYSEMV and an EMC-Workbench with advanced cable and source models are the first steps for an efficient EMC-optimization. The function and integration of these tools will be discussed with a burst analysis on a part of a defined simple standard system.

articleTitle: A Fresh Look at Channel Assignment in Uniform Networks
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Uniform networks provide a setting in which channel assignment strategies may be studied in detail. When there are constraints not only on channel re-use, but also on the assignment of neighbouring channels, then it is, in general, difficult to identify assignments that are optimal in the sense of using as few channels as possible. This paper assembles a suite of twenty test problems and uses them to evaluate both established assignment algorithms and possible alternatives. A distinction is drawn between problems that call for a single channel at each site and those that demand multiple coverage.

articleTitle: Radiated Electromagnetic Emission Prediction using a Current Probe
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this paper we are going to present a new radiated emission prediction method for equipments with relatively long interface cables by using cable current measurement techniques. It takes into account the current distribution waveform on the cable, the current fluctuation, the image effect of the cable, the emission maximization procedure at the Open Area Test Site (OATS) as well as the radiation pattern of the receiving antenna. It is proved to be a useful diagnostic tool to predict the electromagnetic emission from long cable equipments.

articleTitle: Specification of Alternative Test Sites With Respect to Given EMC Field Standards
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: During the last years a lot of new test facilities have been presented which claim to be in accordance with standard test procedures. The intention of this paper is to show a way to relate the standardized procedures to the new alternative methods. As an example the most referenced standard for field immunity measurement the IEC 1000-4-3 is used. At first the main goals for insuring reproducible field conditions are extracted from this standard and are discussed in this paper. For the main goal "field homogeneity" a modified procedure is presented. The field strength can be calculated as a deterministic value. In this paper deviations of the field strength from a mean are considered as statistical errors. This leads to a more general definition of the field uniformity. Two configurations of test sites requested by IEC 1000-4-3 are studied with this statistical but more general approach. The paper stresses the point of field uniformity and the problems of its definition. A recommendation for a novel and more versatile definition is given. Finally some hints on error limits considering polarisation of the field vector and far field condition are given.

articleTitle: EMC: An Educational Challenge
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Among the many interesting aspects of electromagnetic compatibility (EMC), the education of EMC engineers is gaining more and more importance throughout the EMC community. A through education of an EMC engineer requires both theoretical and practical aspects including EMC measurement equipment and procedures. In the session “EMC EDUCATION” seven outstanding contributions will widely discuss these and others themes.

articleTitle: Circuit Oriented EM Modeling Techniques for EMC
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Computer oriented EM programs play an important part in the EMC design of modern electronic equipment. The hardware to be modeled is becoming more complex and the frequency ranges of interest are continuously increasing. This increase in the frequencies involved makes the design of such equipment more difficult. Circuit oriented computer techniques and programs are gaining in popularity since they lead to more useful and understandable solutions and techniques. In this paper we summarize the recent progress in circuit oriented techniques for the Electro Magnetic Modeling (EMM) of electronic equipment and VLSI circuitry. Both differential and integral equation based models are examined as they pertain to this session on circuit oriented EM modeling.

articleTitle: Automatic Signal Integrity Analysis of Complex Systems
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The post layout signal integrity analysis of complex digital circuits gains more and more importance based on miniaturization and increasing processing speed. This contribution shows a first approach to formalize the occuring problem for the automatic evaluation of signal integrity analysis results. Based on these considerations a very first approach realized in the EMC-Workbench [8] for the treatment of the problem will be explained. The contribution finishes with a short discussion of possible improvements.

articleTitle: Designing with Conductive Plastic Compounds for EMI-Shielding
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Part design greatly influences the level of EMI shielding performance attainable with conductive plastic housing. Considerations for the designer of a shielded plastic enclosure include: frequencies to be attenuated, level of noise reduction/shielding required, part configuration, manufacture and assembly, cosmetics as well as physical performance requirements. Design solutions specific to manufacture and assembly will be presented. Methods for grounding, joining and ventilating conductive thermoplastic housings and their impact on shielding performance will be discussed.

articleTitle: Super Absorbing Conditions for Time-Domain Field Computations: Application to Shield WIDE-Band Characterization
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A time-domain method namely, the transmission-line matrix (TLM) method is used for field computation pertaining to some EMC applications. To make the method more efficient, the perfectly matched layer (PML) technique is interfaced with the TLM algorithm via a finite difference time-domain (FDTD) discretization of PML equations. As a result, the high performance of the absorbing conditions allows one to place the PML interface as close as few tenths of a wavelength to the scatterer. Compared to standard absorbing conditions, the computational volume can be further reduced and, hence, substantial gain in terms of computer expenditure is achieved. The proposed algorithm is validated by comparison with the well established moment method (MoM) and application to a wideband characterization of a shielding enclosure with apertine is presented.

articleTitle: A Thermal and Electrical Model for MO-Arrester Degradation
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In the paper a thermal/ electrical model of one single MO-disk in its geometrical surrounding is developed. Geometrical influences (characterized by R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</inf>) as well as the thermal behaviour of one single disk were taken into account. The influence of ambient temperature θ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">U</inf> and the influence of degradation on the Ρ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">v</inf>-θ-curve were investigated in detail. The P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">V</inf>-θ- curve of the investigated type of disk is approximated with an analytical expression. This approximation is characterized by a temperature factor k<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">θ</inf> that describes the influence of temperature and a degradation factor k<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">D</inf> that describes the degradation of the material. For new disks k<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">D</inf> is 1 whereas for a degraded disk it is higher than 1. The model developed can also be used for complex geometrical constructions. For a high voltage arrester for example many of the models for one disk with changing geometrical parameters have to be put together. The resulting thermal system describes the behaviour of the whole arrester.

articleTitle: A Brief History of EMC Measurements
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Over the last 30 years there have been a great number of changes in both the technology and philosophy of EMC measurements. The papers in this session discuss the latest discoveries and challenges in EMC measurement. In the hope that others will not need to reinvent the wheel, some of the early experiences of the author and his colleagues are given in this introductory paper.

articleTitle: Transient Ground Parameters and Voltage Sources in Time-Domain Modeling of Field-Excited Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: New transient simulation models of the lossy ground return parameters and of the distributed and lumped voltage sources due to an impinging EM plane wave, are described. The proposed expressions are valid in a wide frequency-range, for low ground conductivity and for small incidence angles. The transient formulation is based on the rational approximation of the frequency-domain expressions, which is obtained by using the model-based-parameter-estimation technique. The procedure is particularly suitable for the efficient calculation of time-convolution by recursive schemes. The transient ground parameters and voltage sources are computed for a power line excited by an EMP plane wave for different values of the incidence angle.

articleTitle: IEC1000-4-7 Defines EMC Testing Methods for Harmonic Currents Analysis Per IEC1000-3-2
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility

authors.preferredName: Mathieu R. W. van den Bergh

abstract: The IEC 1000-3-2/3 standards specify EMC evaluation criteria of harmonic currents and Flicker (voltage fluctuations). Both standards cover electrical equipment with currents up to 16 Arms, thus covering the majority of household and small industrial apparatus. The standards specify measurement methods, and analysis techniques. Neither standard is well understood, as evidenced by the many different interpretations. The IEC committee recognized that further clarification of harmonic current, and voltage fluctuations analysis, are required. A task force (IEC-TC77A/WG1/TF02) was organized, undertaking the first step of this clarification process, in the form of a revised IEC 1000-4-7 standard. This document defines the new reference instrument for harmonic analysis. The revision of this important standard was agreed upon during the task force meeting of July, 1996. The document has been submitted for approval, via the regular IEC channels. Expedient approval is expected. This paper discusses the new IEC 1000-4-7 standard.

articleTitle: Frequency Limitations in Photonic EMF Probes
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper shows the frequency limitations of photonic electromagnetic field (EMF) probes. Firstly it shows the measuring errors due to integration of measured EMF by a probe, secondly resonant phenomena in the probe are discussed and the frequency limitations due to resonances of parasitic reactances in the probe are investigated Theoretical considerations of piezoelectric phenomena in electro optical crystals are presented and experimentally confirmed. The latter may limit the frequency band the most rigorously. An upper corner frequency of photonic sensors is estimated around several GHz.

articleTitle: Let's Make the Compatibility Requirements Compatible
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A structure for a necessary harmonization of the numerous EMC standards in the world is described. Existing test methods and test equipment of different standards are combined to serve as a baseline for the development of a unified EMC test standard for all applications. A discussion on test limits is set aside until an agreement on test methods is reached.

articleTitle: Surges and Transients
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Introductory paper to the session “Surges and Transients” of the 12th International Zurich Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility

articleTitle: A Set of Tutorial Shielding Experiments
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A pedagogic concept for introducing engineering students to the basic phenomena of shielding against electric and magnetic fields is presented. It consists in demonstrating experiments, explaining the physical background and instructing the students on how to verify the experimental results by calculation.

articleTitle: Low Frequency Gradientometer for EMC Certification
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) certification process needs to investigate the radiation sources possibly existing in the tested equipment. It is a serious problem in low and very low frequency domain which, to our knowledge, has not yet been solved. An attempt to develop the methodology and corresponding hardware implementation was undertaken. The theoretical approach to the solution of the problem with the help of one-component search-coil magnetometer-gradientometer was made. The problems of hardware manufacturing are discussed and the results of practical implementation are shortly presented.

articleTitle: Discrete Circuit Element Modeling of Complex Impedances in Partial Element Description Networks
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The authors have developed a technique that allows one to automatically derive simple full wave equivalent lumped networks for general planar interconnection discontinuities. In this technique, we start from a so called partial element description (PED) of the given structure, which is a network interpretation of the numerical analysis of the given structure, analogous to Ruehli’s PEEC method. When we use full wave Greens functions, the impedances in the PED networks are complex and frequency dependent. In this paper, we will discuss a technique that allows one to model these impedances using only real and frequency independent discrete circuit elements.

articleTitle: A New Strategy for the Calculation of Radiation and EMI by Successive Cross-Coupling Computations
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper presents a new fast method for calculating current distributions and radiation in a configuration of wires and other geometry elements. It is shown that it approximates the solution received by the Method of Moments, but needs remarkably less computation time, especially for complex geometries. This is done by considering the successive cross-couplings between the geometry elements until the influence of the single induction process is negligible.

articleTitle: One Year of Experience With the EMC Directive
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The entering into force of the EMC Directive on the 1st January 1996 was already postponed for four years due to the lack of product standards on emission and on immunity for a great number of products and due to the lack of knowledge of manufacturers of the immunity characteristics of their products.

articleTitle: Improving the Statistical Evaluation of Immunity to Electrical Transients
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Due to stochastic properties of immunity test results against electrical transients major problems are their evaluation in respect to the immunity of the equipment under test (EUT) in a prospected environment. Employing stochastic system theory this paper provides a comprehensive statistical model for assessing an EUT’s immunity in an electromagnetic environment, i.e. to compute probability of malfunctions as well as associated costs.

articleTitle: Using Incandescent Lamp Failure Levels for Assessment of the Surge Environment
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper reports a joint investigation of the failure modes and levels of incandescent lamps (“light bulbs”) exposed to surges occurring in low-voltage AC power systems. Tests were performed in one European laboratory and in one U.S. laboratory on typical 100-W bulbs used in the two environments, the North American 120-V systems, and the 230-V European systems. Through complementary tests and high-speed video observation of the flashes, more detailed understanding of the parameters has been obtained. Having determined what it takes to fail a light bulb by a surge, this information can be used to assess the surge environment by noting that frequent bulb failures do not occur, therefore surges above the failure threshold must be infrequent.

articleTitle: Capacitive Clamp Used in Standards; Analysis of Test Method and New Results
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This article is based on the critical analysis of the standard EMC test procedures using capacitive clamp (ISO 7637-3, IEC 1000-4-4,...)· It gives new results based on the time observation of the coupling phenomena simulated by the capacitive clamp. It also offers a synthesis of the results not currently included in standard documents. It reflects on the suitability of the suggested test pulse levels in the standard procedures. It also points out the existence in certain cases, of an incorrect correlation between the capacitive and inductive coupling simulated by the capacitive clamp and an actual electromagnetic cross-talk observed between a victim and a polluter cable. Many practical results not specified in the standardization, are given in this article, namely about the effects of the impedance conditions of the D.U.T. (Device Under Test) on the coupling simulation by capacitive clamp.

articleTitle: Enhancement of the Immunity of a Radiometry Imaging System Against High Energy Disturbances
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The problem of radiometry imaging system immunity enchancement by means of signal processing is considered as the solution of the inverse ill-posed problem. The proposed method makes use of the iterative technique with constrains on the solution and adaptive regularization procedure. Due to the nonlinearity of the method which is able to solve the problem of bandlimited extrapolation, the possibility appears to improve the quality of the radiometry images.

articleTitle: Sampling of PCB Near Fields - Calculation of Far Fields
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A method for measuring the currents on a printed circuit board (PCB) has been developed. The magnetic field strength above the board is scanned by small probes. This information can be used to calculate the current distribution on the printed circuit board. The numerical backtransformation is based on the Method of Moments and uses Maxwell’s equations. This inverse problem is inherently ill-posed and leads to an ill-conditioned system of linear equations which is solved by the conjugate gradient method. The calculated currents build the starting point for the calculation of the far field produced by the PCB.

articleTitle: Numerical Analysis of Errors Associated With Antenna Calibration and Emission Testing
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The antenna factor of an antenna must be known in order to perform EMC emission tests. Usually a near-held antenna factor is involved. After deriving a relation between gain and antenna factor, we compare several possible definitions of a nearfield gain and the related near-field antenna factor including the standard site method. These comparisons are based on numerical experiments using the method of moments which offers some advantages as compared to measurements. Emission testing is also investigated where we compare the radiated fields from an interference source computed directly with the field strength values obtained by numerically simulating the measuring process using for instance the standard site method.

articleTitle: An Instructional Program Based on Partial-Element Equivalent Circuits (PEEC) Used to Demonstrate EMC Design Concepts
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A properly trained EMC engineer must fully understand the nature of the distribution of the currents flowing in a structure. However, creating practical experiments that demonstrate the characteristics of current flow is not easy due to the difficulty of measuring distributed currents. This presentation describes the development and user operation of a simulation program that runs on a personal computer that can be used to demonstrate important EMC design concepts. Students can use the program as a "laboratory" to verify the theory behind return current flow and the causes of common-mode current and to gain an intuitive understanding of the factors that influence the way current is distributed. Some example exercises that use the program are given.

articleTitle: Measurement of Magnetic Near Fields on Printed Circuit Boards by using a Magnetic Loop Antenna
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Magnetic near fields on a ground plane of a printed circuit board (PCB) are studied. The fields are measured by using a small loop antenna with a termination load. The property of the probe is discussed by comparing a conventional loop antenna with a short circuit. Performance of the probe is confirmed by comparing the calculated and the measured values for a PCB. Magnetic field profiles of PCBs are studied in varions standpoints. Experimental results show that the fields on an upper and a reverse sides of the ground plane of finite area have different profiles especially when a trace pattern is set near the edge of the board. The field magnitude on the reverse side is so large that common-mode emissions may be generated through an interconnected ground wire.

articleTitle: Skin Effect Influence in a Direct Stroke to the Lightning Protection System of Buildings
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Skin effect is often neglected for the calculation of the transient current distribution on the lightning protection of buildings. Firstly, this paper outlines a time domain computational method to model skin effect in ground return bare conductors. This method is successfully applied to two types of conductors. Secondly, the lightning current distribution on a typical lightning protection system is computed with and without skin effect. The comparison of these two results shows that skin effect influence can not be neglected for fast transients and large permeability materials.

articleTitle: Treatment of Geometrically Thin Single and Multi-Layers by the Method of Moments
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The integral equation formalism in conjunction with the method of moments has proved to be an efficient tool for the computation of fields in a broad variety of technical configurations. In the case of field penetration through geometrically thin, non-ideal single or multi-layered surfaces (screening problems) it is necessary to account for the real, generally very complicated current distribution within each layer. Discretizing a layer for example using volume elements would lead to severe numerical difficulties. Defining a simple surface impedance also leads to unacceptable results. In this paper a procedure will be presented which combines known analytical solutions with the integral equation method. The introduced technique is computationally effective and applicable to configurations, which can be treated by surface current modeling. Wires or wire-grid structures can be regarded in addition.

articleTitle: The Repeatability and Calibration Consistency of a New Electric Field Source
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper describes a new spherical dipole electric field source that creates an electric field that is extremely repeatable, stable and accurate. Using this source, accurate comparisons and calibrations of different test environments can now be made easily. The results in this paper show a source repeatability of better than 5 dB across the frequency range of 10 MHz to 2 GHz. Calibration consistency over a period of 6 months is shown as well as radiated electric field strength unit-to-unit consistency. Traditional methods to generate electric fields to calibrate measurement sites or to compare different types of measurement sites (GTEM, OATS, TEM cell, anechoic room, semi-anechoic room, etc.) have always been limited to the accuracy of the RF generator and transmit antenna (typically 2-4 dB at best). The significantly better accuracy of this source makes these measurements much more accurate and useful.

articleTitle: An Integrated Optical E-Field Sensor using a Reflection Scheme
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A new integrated optical E-fleld sensor with a reflection scheme is presented. In comparison with previously developed sensors the optical fibres have only to be connected at one end of the sensor chip. Thus E-field measurements in hard-to-get-at spaces becomes possible, for example due to dipping this reflection sensor in ventilating louvres of a device. Furthermore measurement errors caused by Fabry-Perot resonances in the used electro optical modulator chip could be reduced from ± 66 % of previously developed modulators up to ± 12 % with a new reflection scheme yielding a stability improvement of a reflection sensor.

articleTitle: EMC Test and Measurement on Printed Circuit Boards
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The consideration of EMC-related aspects is often not part of the traditional design process (layout, prototyping, production). Faster technologies in combination with increasing clock frequencies, higher packing density and increasing complexity of electronic designs force manufacturers to extend their design process. Regarding economical aspects (time to market, first time right) EMC-constrained design becomes more important, too. Measurement techniques are an approved method to analyse and solve EMC-problems. This paper presents several examples of signal integrity (SI) and radiation measurements. A computer aided measurement equipment is used to achieve high performance in generating and handling measurement data. Measurement control and data storage is done by a PC via IEEE 488.2 bus. For downstream operations the transfer of measured data via ethernet to the connected workstations is possible. ’X-Window’ applications can be used for detailed comparison of measurement and simulation results.

articleTitle: Modelling and Statistical Analysis of the Lightning Effects on Electricity Supply and Telecommunication Lines
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to present a numerical tool for the statistical analysis of over voltages induced on a power or telecommunication line by an indirect or a direct lightning strike. The model is based on the use of EMTP software combined with a Monte Carlo approach. Comparison of the theoretical results is made with measurements carried out on real installations.

articleTitle: Introduction to the Partial Element Equivalent Circuit Method for the Electromagnetic Modeling of Three Dimensional Geometries
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: • PEEC Model Derivations/Simplification: Part 1 Introduction PEEC Model Derivation Model Discretization External Fields and Circuit Equation Formulations Macromodeling by Model Simplifications

articleTitle: Distributed-Source Transmission Line Theory for Electromagnetic Induction Studies
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: With the inclusion of distributed sources, transmission line theory can be used to investigate electromagnetic induction in long conductors such as power systems, pipelines, and phone cables. Previous work has studied transmission lines with “passive” terminations, ie those with an impedance component only. This work extends the theory to include “active” terminations which comprise a voltage source in series with an impedance. This allows the theory to be applied to networks represented by multiple transmission lines. At a junction between lines, the termination seen by one line can now be represented by a Thevenin equivalent circuit for induction in the other line. The full expressions for current and voltage along a transmission line of arbitrary length are presented. It is also shown how simplified expressions can be obtained for long or short transmission lines.

articleTitle: The Sensitivity of Channel Assignment to Constraint Specification
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: We show that in assigning channels to transmitters in a regular network, to satisfy a given signal-to-interference ratio (SIR), care should be taken in the choice of constraints used to specify the problem. In particular, we consider the constraints in terms of minimum distances for channel re-use and adjacent channel use. We show that it is possible to meet a SIR requirement with various sets of such constraints, leading to possible channel assignments with widely differing spectral requirements. Hence care is needed in constraint specification to avoid wasting spectrum. We also show that, for the simply constructed assignments we consider here, abandoning such constraints can lead to even more efficient use of spectrum; each assignment is then assessed directly by the SIR it can achieve over a fixed region.

articleTitle: Evaluations of Microcontroller Susceptibility to Impulsive Electromagnetic Disturbances
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The results of an investigation on microcontroller susceptibility to impulsive disturbances described in this paper show that the susceptibility depends directly on the microcontroller’s operational functions, especially on the microinstructions used for an assembler instruction. As a result, the fault frequency can change within some nanoseconds between 0% and 100%.

articleTitle: Traceable Antenna Calibrations by using a Reference Antenna
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: We have developed a set of precision dipoles to be used as standards for antenna calibration. A broadband transfer standard antenna can be calibrated against these reference dipoles by a substitution method. The transfer standard can then be used to trace the calibration of other antennas to national standards. By application of time-domain gating the method allows a total uncertainty of less than 0.3 dB for antennas with an omnidirectional pattern in the H-plane and of 0.5 dB for a typical logarithmic-periodic dipole antenna, both at a confidence level of 95.5 % at frequencies up to 1 GHz. This is significantly better than the uncertainty that can be achieved by applying the standard site method.

articleTitle: On the Effects of RF Interference in Voltage Regulator Integrated Circuits
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Voltage Regulators built in bipolar technology shows high susceptibility in case of RF interferences directly applied on the regulated output port. On the other hand the Modified Gummel Poon Model (MGPM) filled into the SPICE simulator allows to evaluate the B JT dc quiescent operating point shift due to RF disturbance directly applied on the device base emitter junction. In order to find out the RF distribution among the integrated active devices, the AC SPICE analysis is performed and the results supplied to the MGPM that is used for the most stressed transistors only. By MGPM, OP, DC and TRAN analysis are carried out for the evaluation of complex ICs behaviour.

articleTitle: Numerical Simulation of a GTEM-Cell
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The modeling process for a numerical simulation of a GTEM-cell is presented. For a sufficient accuracy of calculation the feeding section, transmission line geometry and hybrid termination must be modeled correctly. Missing from recent papers is the modeling of a feeding section with very low mismatch and the modeling of the resistance termination boards with their optimized profile in two directions. Both elements have essential influences on the accuracy of the whole model. Comparisons of calculated results with measurements in a commercial GTEM-cell are presented. The generated model is applicable to various further investigations.

articleTitle: Crest Factor Sensor for Electromagnetic Fields
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper presents anew instrument suitable for measuring the crest factor of EM fields having arbitrary waveform, unknown polarization and direction of propagation. The instrument is based upon the simultaneous detection in isotropic mode of both the peak value and the RMS value of the EM field. The ratio of these two measurements is the measure of the crest factor. This instrument is particularly useful for EMC and Radiation Hazard usages, as it allows a more complete characterization of the EM fields. A prototype and some experimental measurements of electric field are included.

articleTitle: Lemp Calculation using an Improved Return Stroke Model
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Using and improved lightning return stroke model the radiated electromagnetic field is calculated, in time and frequency domain, above Earth surface. The case of the perfectly conducting ground is treated. The proposed model (PM) is based on the existence of the travelling current source and the mechanism of the lightning channel discharge according to the Travelling Current Source (TCS) and Diendorfer-Uman (DU) models. It enables entire separation of the channel-base current and charge distribution along the lightning channel. The PM can give considerable difference as in the current maximum at some height as well as in the maximum of the current slope <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$dt(z, t) /dt\vert_{max}$</tex>, compared with the previously established TCS and DU model. Similar behavior is noticed for the electromagnetic field. The different influences on the charge distribution in the channel might be tested to obtain better fitting of the theoretical results with the experimental data of radiated electromagnetic pulse in the time and frequency domain. Further, the internal channel processes can be partially examined during the return stroke. These results might be used for correct estimation of LEMP as well as for the better understanding of the gaseous-physical processes in the lightning channel during the return stroke.

articleTitle: Quasistationary Conductive Effects in Coupled Underground Cables
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper presents a method of the solution for the voltages between the sheaths and cable conductors excited along conductively and inductively coupled cables by conductive effects of complex earthing arrangements. It is assumed that the system considered is linear and that the earth is an isotropic, homogeneous medium of finite conductivity. The transmission line model of the conductor with earth return, a segmental linear approximation of the curve of the primary potential distribution along the cables and the concept of superposition have been used in the method. It should be pointed out that the method does not require the numerical integration. The method may be useful for evaluation of quasistationary conductive effects on buried cables in many practical cases, which are connected with power supply systems, electric traction and cathodic protection as well. The technical application of the method presented is illustrated by an example.

articleTitle: The Use of Wire-Grid Structures in the Combined Analyses of Mom and GTD/UTD
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: An extension of the Method of Moments (MoM) with the Uniform Geometrical Theory of Diffraction (UTD) is described in this paper. Introducing specific types of field sources makes it possible to use the linear antenna structures and the wire grid models of MoM in the combination with UTD. This combination is called Hybrid Method (HM). A new class of applications can be investigated in combining both methods. With the HM it is possible to calculate arrangements containing both electrically small and large bodies.

articleTitle: Relevance of Formal and Nonformal EMC Education in India
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The first part of this paper outlines a formal undergraduate level EMC course which is offered in six Institutes of Technologies (IITs) and a few Universities in India for the students interested in electromagnetic compatibility engineering. The second part of the paper emphasises on the importance of nonformal EMC education like "EMC Distance Education and Open Learning" to produce skilled manpower to look after EMC design and measurement techniques in various export-oriented electronic industries.

articleTitle: ELF Tweek Sferics: Direction Finding, Propagation Mechanism and Location of Lightning Discharges
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Detailed wave characteristics (incident and azimuthal angles, wave polarization, and their frequency dependences) of tweek sferics have been elucidated on the basis of the application of our field-analysis direction finding to VLF data observed in South China. It is then found that the wave polarization of the 1st-order mode at the frequency above its cutoff frequency (f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1c</inf>= 1.7 ∼ 1.8kHz) is always lefthanded and it becomes exactly left-handed circular when the wave frequency decreases down to the f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1c</inf>, together with the fact the incident angle becomes zero (vertical) when the frequency approaches f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1c</inf>. Whereas, the Oth-order mode at frequency below f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1c</inf> is found to be linearly polarized. These wave propagation characteristics are first interpreted qualitatively, and then we try to explain them in terms of the full wave theory in the Earth-ionosphere waveguide in which the realistic electron density profiles of the lower ionosphere are assumed. Finally, we suggest that our field-analysis direction finding free from the polarization error should be adopted for the accurate direction finding of lightning discharges.

articleTitle: Modeling of Integrated Circuits to Support SI-Analysis
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this paper methods for modeling of digital circuits with respect to signal integrity analysis will be presented. These model structures allow a separate description of the input and output-behavior with various accuracy.

articleTitle: Electrical Characterization of Anisotropic Transmission Line Systems With a Hybrid FEM/BEM Method
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this paper, a hybrid FEM/BEM approach for solving Maxwell’s equations in the frequency domain is presented. The method can be applied to uniform transmission lines and waveguides containing anisotropic and lossy media. Based on a rigorous full-wave analysis, frequency-dependent propagation constants and electromagnetic fields can be obtained. Spurious solutions which usually appear when applying a double-curl formulation in combination with linear, nodal finite elements, are avoided by requiring the magnetic field to have zero divergence. A numerical procedure is presented which enables the solution of the nonlinear equation for the propagation constant resulting from the combined application of FEM and BEM. This procedure is also capable of handling degenerate modes.

articleTitle: Extraction of Layout Data as a Basis for EMC-Analysis of PCB
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In order to support signal integrity and radiation analysis of Printed Circuit Boards (PCBs), the layout data has to be extracted from the layout description in an automatical manner. The data has to be extented by electrical and simulation parameters and by model descriptions for the integrated components. At last it is passed to the different simulation programs. This paper describes the relevant requirements of such an extraction and pre-processing step. The architecture for such a software is discussed. A special task in this process is to choose suited data structures.

articleTitle: Radiated Emissions From a Digital Switching Exchange Due to PCBS, Cables and Small Apertures
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: When physically large systems, such as a digital switching exchange for high speed broad band applications, must be tested in order to comply with the EN 55022 standard for radiated emission some problems arise. This paper deals with these problems. Simple closed formulas to predict radiated emissions from elementary sources such as ICs and tracks in PCBs, cables and small apertures are outlined with their limits of application. The models were verified by measurements.

articleTitle: Report on the URSI Commission E Scientific Activities for the Period 1994-1996
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This triennium report was prepared by V. Scuka, and was revised by M. Hayakawa. We, Commission Members, would like to thank Dr. Scuka for his great efforts in organizing this report and also for his dedication to Commission E activity.

articleTitle: Lightning Electromagnetic Effects on Lines and Cables
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The widespread use of sensitive electronic devices has increased the interest on transients, in particular those caused by lightning (direct and/or indirect). This tutorial presents the latest developments in modelling the electromagnetic (indirect) effects of lightning. The progress in field-to-transmission lines coupling calculations for networks permits the analysis of more complicated structures submitted to a lightning electromagnetic field. Combined approaches using low frequency coupling expressions which neglect the propagation in the case of complicated circuits but with small dimensions will be discussed. Such approaches can give approximative solutions and orders of magnitude helpful for a correct EMC design for very complex configurations like for instance control and protection circuits in power network substations

articleTitle: Aspects of EMC at the Equipment Level
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The existence of unwanted electro-magnetic (EM) interactions between electric and electronic equipment (or systems, sub-assemblies, devices) and, in particular the prevention of those interactions, forces us to pay attention to electromagnetic compatibility (EMC). In its basic form, such an unwanted interaction or electro-magnetic interference (EMI) problem, can be described by the well-known EMI triptych consisting of a source of EM disturbance, a coupling path and a victim circuit. The triptych can be considered at four levels: (1) system level (2) equipment or subsystem level (3) sub-assembly or printed wiring board level, and (4) device or component level. This tutorial paper addresses Level (2): the equipment or subsystem level, as it is also the level where most of the statutory (as forced by the legislator) operational requirements (as forced by the equipment user) apply. Since the four levels are not independent, the adjacent Level (1) and Level (3) will be considered when necessary. In this paper the emphasis will be on understanding of the various phenomena.

articleTitle: Estimation of an Electromagnetic Emission Ability
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Often numerical methods are applied in order to obtain some information of a practical design with respect to its ability to radiate electromagnetic energy already during the layout phase. Usually, this not only implies quite time consuming calculations, but as well very involved modelling techniques, since in general, practical designs are much to complex to analyse the compound of structures simultaneously in one big sweep. In the following focus will be on printed circuit boards and an approach will be presented which attempts to avoid a great deal of the complex operations by using a classification scheme to reduce the amount of data one is confronted with. This classification may be applied to functional entities separately and once this is performed, a first indication of the capability of a design to radiate may easily be provided. From there on, one may proceed either towards a more detailed analysis, where for instance a set of rules may be applied to weight the classified structures accordingly, or inspect the substructures with more sophisticated numerical tools. However, on occasion it will be advantageous to introduce some modifications already at the classification stage in order to mitigate prospective problems.

articleTitle: Rule-Driven EMC-Routing
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: To avoid EMC problems from the beginning and to render the design process as efficient as possible, EMC design criteria have to be integrated directly into all design phases. In this article a design environment is described which, in conjunction with the placement tools described in [SS97], makes it possible to control the whole layout design process by EMC design rules. If EMC rules are chosen appropriately, many EMC problems will be avoided from the beginning. The design environment includes a rich and comfortable set of rule classes, methods for efficient and flexible rule specification and administration, rule check facilities and intelligent routing algorithms, which consider the rules directly during routing.

articleTitle: URSI Lille General Assembly Report
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The URSI 25th General Assembly was held in Lille, France during the period of August 28 to September 5, 1996. The GA was very successful due to the great efforts of the local organization, Past Commission E chair (Prof. Scuka), session chairs etc. In the following I include the reports of Commission E sessions and several joint sessions (reported by session chairs(s)).

articleTitle: Methods and Tools to Support the Design of Components and Systems Under EMC-Constraints
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The term EMC (Electromagnetic Compatibility) includes, as generally might be known, all actions intended to eliminate electromagnetic interference in electronic systems. Challenges faced in the microelectronic area include growing system complexity, higher operating speed, denser design at all levels of integration (chip, printed circuit board, MCM and system). Growing complexity, denser design and higher speed all lead to a substantial increase in EMC problems and design time. EMC is not commonly accepted in microelectronic design. Microelectronic designers have the opinion that EMC has to do with electrical and electronic systems and mandatory product regulations instead of requirements to the integrated circuit they are designing. In this contribution a general overview of the state of the art, future requirements and development trends with respect to the design and the application of integrated circuits considering EMC-constraints will be presented. A concept for an EMC-adequate electronic system design will be introduced. This concept is based on a generalized development process to integrate EMC-constraints into system design. A prototype of an ’integrated’ EMC-development environment will be introduced. Based on this strategy the generation of user specific design and analysis environments including various set of EMC-tools is possible.

articleTitle: The Fast and Efficient Computation of Capacitance Coefficients of Multiconductor Structures for EMC Purposes with a Parallelizied 3D-BEM
publicationTitle: 12th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: We present a method for fast computation of capacitance coefficients of arbitrary multiconductor structures in the presence of any dielectric material with a parallel 3D-Boundary Element Method (BEM). Starting with theoretical basics of the algorithm an implementation is presented which has been adopted to parallel execution on shared memory multiprocessor-workstations and networks of workstations. Runtime numbers and examples are given.
